notes.text:
Local analytic lemmas.

Write D=i partial barpartial/(2 pi). All representatives below are the actual upper semicontinuous representatives. No mass or envelope theorem is imported.

1. Elementary analytic facts.

For a smooth real function f, Df>=0 is equivalent to positivity of its mixed complex derivative matrix. On a complex line with direction xi, the real Laplacian of its restriction is four times the corresponding Hermitian quadratic form. For a C2 function g on a complex disk,

  average_{|z|=r} g-g(0)
    =(1/(2 pi)) integral_{|z|<r} log(r/|z|) Delta g(z) dA(z).

Thus positive complex Hessian implies every line disk mean inequality. Conversely, second-order expansion of circle means gives positivity of all line Laplacians. Upper semicontinuity and these line inequalities are the local submean definition of psh used here; identically negative infinite line restrictions are permitted.

For locally integrable psh f, convolution with a nonnegative smooth radial approximate identity preserves the disk inequalities, by integrating their translates. The convolutions are smooth, so their complex Hessians are positive. Their L1 convergence gives Df>=0 as a current.

Psh functions also satisfy the real ball mean inequality: average the line circle inequalities over unit directions to obtain the sphere inequality, then integrate radially. Consequently, at EVERY point,

  f(x)=lim_{r decreasing to 0} average_{B(x,r)} f.

The inequality from below follows from the ball mean inequality. Upper semicontinuity gives the inequality from above. At a point with value negative infinity, nearby values lie below any prescribed finite number on a sufficiently small neighborhood, so the averages tend to negative infinity. The same proof applies to radial convolution, which is a nonnegative mixture of spherical averages.

If a genuine quasi-psh f has Df>=0 as a current, write f=p+a locally, with p psh and a smooth. Radial convolution converges to p canonically at every point, and to a in the ordinary sense. Hence f_epsilon converges pointwise to f, including negative infinite values. Current positivity makes f_epsilon smooth with positive complex Hessian on smaller domains. Their disk inequalities pass to f by reverse Fatou: they share a finite upper bound on the compact neighborhood in question. Therefore f itself is psh. This does not permit upward point spikes in a representative.

Suppose genuine quasi-psh f_N decrease, have a common local bound Df_N>=-A omega, where omega=D|z|^2, and converge in L1 to a limit finite almost everywhere. Then f_N+A|z|^2 are psh. Their actual pointwise limit is upper semicontinuous, since an infimum of upper semicontinuous functions is upper semicontinuous. Disk inequalities pass by monotone convergence applied to a common upper bound minus the functions. The limit is therefore proper psh after the same quadratic addition, and current inequalities pass by L1 convergence. This proves genuineness of the ACTUAL decreasing limit, without replacing its values on a null set.

Two canonical quasi-psh functions equal almost everywhere are equal everywhere. Add one common positive quadratic locally so both are psh; their ball averages agree, and the preceding recovery identity identifies every value. The same argument upgrades an almost-everywhere inequality to an everywhere inequality between canonical quasi-psh functions.

The maximum of two psh functions is psh: at a center use the disk inequality of a member attaining the maximum, whose circle values are bounded by the maximum. A convex increasing composition preserves disk inequalities by Jensen, whenever defined and upper semicontinuous. This can first be applied to finite truncations.

Positive convex combinations of genuine h-psh functions are genuine h-psh functions. They are canonically quasi-psh, and for nonnegative weights summing to one,

  h+D(sum a_k f_k)=sum a_k(h+Df_k)>=0.

Negative infinite values in positive-weight sums remain negative infinite; a zero coefficient contributes zero. Constant shifts preserve the same properties.

2. Exact upper-envelope inequality for a nonclosed background.

Let theta be ANY smooth real (1,1)-form, possibly nonclosed and nonpositive. Let A be a nonempty family of genuine theta-psh functions, locally uniformly bounded above, with a proper locally integrable lower member a. Put S=sup_{v in A}v and Q=S*. Then Q is genuine quasi-psh and theta+DQ>=0 exactly.

On a coordinate ball choose a constant real Hermitian form H dominating theta. There is a real quadratic q_H with Dq_H=H. For every v in A,

  D(v+q_H)=(Dv+theta)+(H-theta)>=0,

so v+q_H is genuine psh by the preceding argument.

Here is the needed upper-supremum proof. For a locally upper-bounded family of psh functions write R for its raw supremum. At a center x with R*(x) finite, choose x_k approaching x and members f_k with f_k(x_k) approaching R*(x). Apply their disk inequalities to a fixed direction and radius, translating the centers to x_k. On their circles f_k<=R*. Reverse Fatou, the common finite upper bound, and upper semicontinuity give

  R*(x)<=average_on_circle R*(x+r exp(i t)xi).

At a negative infinite center the inequality is automatic. The lower member and upper bound ensure local integrability and properness. Thus R* is psh. Adding a smooth quadratic commutes with regularization, so Q+q_H is psh and DQ>=-H.

To recover the EXACT variable-form bound, fix a chart and omega=D|z|^2. For each epsilon>0 and center x choose a neighborhood U_x on which

  -epsilon omega<=theta(y)-theta(x)<=epsilon omega.

Then H_x=theta(x)+epsilon omega is constant and

  theta<=H_x<=theta+2 epsilon omega.

The constant-form argument gives theta+DQ>=-2 epsilon omega on U_x. Localize any compactly supported positive (n-1,n-1) test form using a nonnegative partition of unity subordinate to a finite such cover. Sum the local inequalities, then let epsilon decrease to zero. This proves theta+DQ>=0 as a current. The local quadratic additions already prove genuine quasi-psh regularity. No local potential for theta was assumed, and no error remains.

If every member is <= continuous F, regularization remains <=F at every point. When theta=h is positive, constants are h-psh. Thus the unrestricted envelope H_F=P_h(F) satisfies

  min_X F<=H_F<=F<=max_X F,
  h+DH_F>=0

canonically everywhere, and is bounded and genuine.

These are ordinary proofs from disk means, convolution, current limits, Jensen and elementary measure convergence. Every distribution/convolution use concerns a locally integrable function by hypothesis or direct estimates. No external mathematical premise or earlier proof is imported. No Monge-Ampere product or mass conclusion follows from this note.

notes.text:
Actual construction and ordinary relative order: A and B.

Fix the stated connected compact complex X of dimension n>=1, smooth positive Hermitian h, smooth positive probability dV, any prescribed nonempty finite or countably infinite set {x_j}, and 0<beta<beta'<1. Enumerate from j=1. Choose the specified finite atlas with larger coordinate charts and a uniform bound dV<=A d lambda in all used coordinate regions. Choose any permitted balls B_j=B(z_j,r_j), with 0<r_j<=1. They may overlap. Choose the single prescribed smooth cutoff, equal to one on |z|<rho_0 and supported in |z|<rho_1, where 0<rho_0<rho_1<1.

On B_j put L_j=1-log(|z-z_j|^2/r_j^2), chi_j=chi((z-z_j)/r_j), and phi_{j,p}=-chi_j L_j^p for p=beta,beta'. Extend by zero outside B_j and assign the actual center value negative infinity. L_j>=1 wherever used; no logarithm outside B_j is evaluated.

Near the center the cutoff equals one. The function f_p(t)=-(1-t)^p on t<=0 satisfies

  f_p'(t)=p(1-t)^(p-1)>0,
  f_p''(t)=p(1-p)(1-t)^(p-2)>0.

Writing zeta=z-z_j, the mixed derivative matrix of log(|zeta|^2/r_j^2) away from zero has entries

  delta_kl/|zeta|^2-(bar zeta_k)zeta_l/|zeta|^4,

and is positive semidefinite. Its genuine pole extension follows by decreasing smooth regularizations log((|zeta|^2+epsilon)/r_j^2), which have positive complex Hessian and converge locally in L1; logarithmic polar integrability verifies the latter. The finite psh truncations max(log(|zeta|^2/r_j^2),-N) have range <=0. Compose with the convex increasing f_p. These decrease to -L_j^p, which is locally L1 by the estimate below. The decreasing-limit facts of n1 prove that its ACTUAL negative infinite center value is psh.

The profile is smooth on the scaled annulus rho_0 r_j<=|z-z_j|<=rho_1 r_j. Elsewhere it is either psh near the center or zero near the boundary. Positivity of h and compactness of this annulus provide a finite K_{j,p}>=0 with

  D phi_{j,p}>=-K_{j,p}h.

Explicitly, take the maximum of zero and the largest negative eigenvalue of D phi_{j,p} relative to h on that annulus. The center region contributes no negative part. Extension across the boundary is smooth because chi_j vanishes on a neighborhood of it. Thus these are genuine quasi-psh profiles.

One common coefficient choice for BOTH exponents is

  delta_j=min(2^(-j), e_j/(1+K_{j,beta}+K_{j,beta'})),
  e_j=2^(-j-2).

It is positive and gives D(delta_j phi_{j,p})>=-e_j h for both exponents. All conclusions below also hold for any other positive coefficients satisfying the stated two lower bounds and delta_j<=2^(-j).

Set a_j=delta_j phi_{j,beta}, c_j=delta_j phi_{j,beta'}, U_N=sum_{j<=N}a_j and W_N=sum_{j<=N}c_j. For a finite set stop at its last index.

Actual countable limits. Let sigma_{2n-1} be the area of the Euclidean unit sphere in real dimension 2n. With y=-log(rho^2/r_j^2), polar integration gives

  integral_{B_j} L_j^p dV
    <= A sigma_{2n-1} r_j^(2n)/2
          integral_0^infinity (1+y)^p exp(-ny)dy
    <= K_1,

  K_1=(A sigma_{2n-1}/2)(1/n+1/n^2).

Here r_j<=1 and (1+y)^p<=1+y. Hence both sums of termwise L1 norms are bounded by K_1 sum_j delta_j<=K_1. The nonpositive partial sums decrease. Monotone convergence of their negatives proves that their ACTUAL pointwise limits u,w are finite almost everywhere, have finite L1 norms and are the L1 limits of the partial sums.

Since sum_{j>=1}e_j=1/4,

  h+DU_N>=(1-sum_{j<=N}e_j)h>=3h/4,
  h+DW_N>=(1-sum_{j<=N}e_j)h>=3h/4.

Locally choose a quadratic q with Dq>=h/4. Then U_N+q and W_N+q are psh. The proper L1 decreasing-limit argument of n1 proves that their actual limits are psh. L1 current passage proves

  u,w<=0,
  h+Du>=3h/4,
  h+Dw>=3h/4.

Thus u,w are proper genuine canonical h-psh functions, not null-set replacements. At x_j, the jth summand is negative infinity, so every later partial sum and the actual limit are negative infinity. Therefore u(x_j)=w(x_j)=-infinity. If the prescribed set is dense, each nonempty open set contains such a point, so u is not locally bounded on any such open set. Additional poles are not excluded.

One fixed w for every rescaling. For 0<t<=1 define

  M_t=sup_{x>=1}(x^beta-t x^beta').

This is finite and nonnegative. Differentiation gives

  M_t=1-t, if t>=beta/beta';
  M_t=(1-beta/beta') (beta/(t beta'))^(beta/(beta'-beta)),
       if 0<t<beta/beta'.

The interior maximizing point is (beta/(t beta'))^(1/(beta'-beta)); at the threshold it equals one and the formulas agree.

At finite points, every partial sum satisfies

  t W_N-U_N
    =sum_{j<=N}delta_j chi_j(L_j^beta-t L_j^beta')
    <=M_t sum_{j<=N}delta_j<=M_t.

At a pole of a finite sum, both corresponding sums are negative infinity, so t W_N<=U_N+M_t is also canonically true there. Also W_N<=U_N because L_j^beta'>=L_j^beta. Taking actual limits yields

  w<=u,
  t w<=u+M_t.

At a pole of u, w is negative infinity by the first inequality, so the second inequality remains true there. If only w is negative infinity it is automatic; otherwise it follows by finite-value passage. Thus t w preceq u for EVERY real 0<t<=1 in the original ordinary order, with the SAME fixed w.

For EVERY b>=1 set v_b=w-bM_{1/b}. This is genuine h-psh, being a constant shift of w, and

  b^(-1)v_b=(1/b)w-M_{1/b}<=u

canonically everywhere. Also u<=0, hence u preceq 0. This proves the ORIGINAL E_env(X,h,0) condition, including common negative infinite values, without subtracting infinite quantities.

These explicit coefficient, polar, current and scalar calculations prove A and B. They require neither separated balls nor a mass condition. Artifact: independent_reconstruction/n2.txt. notes.text:
Countable exponential integrability and exact multiplier ideals: C.

Use the actual functions and coefficient bounds from n2. Fix ANY real s>0 and set p=beta'. Define

  C_s=n/2+(1-p)s(2sp/n)^(p/(1-p)).

For all y>=0,

  s(1+y)^p<=ny/2+C_s.

Indeed, the maximum of sx^p-(n/2)x over x>=0 occurs at x=(2sp/n)^(1/(1-p)) and equals (1-p)s(2sp/n)^(p/(1-p)). Substitute x=1+y. Consequently

  integral_0^infinity exp(s(1+y)^p-ny)dy
    <=(2/n)exp(C_s).

Define f_{j,q}=chi_j L_j^q on B_j, zero outside, for q=beta,beta'; its actual center value is positive infinity. Since q<=p, L_j>=1 and 0<=chi_j<=1, the atlas and polar estimates give the uniform-in-j bound

  integral_X exp(s f_{j,q})dV
    <=1+(A sigma_{2n-1}/2)
             integral_0^infinity exp(s(1+y)^p-ny)dy
    <=K_s,

  K_s=1+(A sigma_{2n-1}/n)exp(C_s)<infinity.

Outside B_j the exponential equals one; inside, r_j^(2n)<=1. Overlapping balls cause no change to this estimate.

For the countable sum choose lambda_j=2^(-j). Then sum lambda_j=1 and delta_j/lambda_j<=1. Jensen with the first N weights and the remaining neutral weight gives

  exp(s sum_{j<=N}delta_j f_{j,q})
    <=1-sum_{j<=N}lambda_j
       +sum_{j<=N}lambda_j exp(s(delta_j/lambda_j)f_{j,q})
    <=1-sum_{j<=N}lambda_j
       +sum_{j<=N}lambda_j exp(s f_{j,q}).

This is needed almost everywhere, where finite terms are finite; the countable prescribed centers have measure zero. Integration bounds the left side by K_s uniformly in N. For q=beta it is exp(-s U_N), and for q=beta' it is exp(-s W_N). These increase to exp(-s u) and exp(-s w) for the ACTUAL limits constructed in n2. Monotone convergence proves

  integral_X exp(-s u)dV<=K_s,
  integral_X exp(-s w)dV<=K_s.

For a finite set use the same finitely many weights and neutral remaining weight. The coefficients and w do not depend on s. Since s was arbitrary, this proves the assertion for EVERY real s>0. It also proves that all poles, including any additional poles of the sums, form measure-zero sets. This is a full countable-sum proof, not an inference from finite partial sums alone or from zero Lelong numbers.

At any point, every holomorphic germ g has a representative bounded on a smaller coordinate neighborhood. Therefore |g|^2 exp(-s u) and |g|^2 exp(-s w) are integrable there. The smooth positive density dV is locally comparable with coordinate Lebesgue measure. Every holomorphic germ consequently belongs to both original multiplier ideals; those ideals contain only holomorphic germs by definition. Hence

  I(su)=O_X,
  I(sw)=O_X

for EVERY real s>0, using exactly exp(-s u), without a changed normalization or a selected valuation family.

The ordinary proof uses the explicit scalar maximum, uniform polar estimate, fixed-weight Jensen and monotone convergence. No external integrability or multiplier-ideal theorem is used. notes.text:
Canonical all-obstacle equality and separate original-completion judgment: D and E.

Fix ANY continuous real F and put m=min_X F, M=max_X F. Let

  H=(sup{v in PSH(X,h), genuine: v<=F})*=P_h(F).

This is the full unrestricted class. Since h is positive, the constant m is a competitor. The exact envelope lemma of n1 gives, canonically everywhere,

  m<=H<=F<=M,
  h+DH>=0.

Thus H is bounded and genuine even when h is nonclosed.

All original ideal competitors. By n3, I(su)=O_X for EVERY real s>0. For ANY genuine h-psh v, I(sv) is a subset of O_X by its definition as holomorphic germs satisfying an integrability condition. Therefore I(sv) is a subset of I(su) for every real s>0, with no restriction on v's singularities. EVERY genuine h-psh v satisfies v preceq_I u. The entire ideal competitor class below F is consequently the unrestricted class, proving

  P_{h,F}[u]_I=H

canonically everywhere. No selected family replaces the original ideal competitors.

Ordinary competitors. Set K=max(0,-m). Then w-K<=m<=H everywhere. For EVERY real 0<t<=1 define

  V_t=(1-t)H+t(w-K),

with a zero coefficient contributing zero. Convexity from n1 gives genuine h-psh regularity; explicitly,

  h+DV_t=(1-t)(h+DH)+t(h+Dw)>=0.

Also V_t<=H<=F at every point. Using n2,

  V_t<=t w+(1-t)M-tK
      <=u+M_t+(1-t)M-tK.

The additive constant is finite for each t. Thus V_t preceq u in the ORIGINAL ordinary order. At any pole of u, w is negative infinity by n2, so the inequality is canonical there too, without subtracting infinite quantities.

Let Q=P_{h,F}[u], still defined using ALL original ordinary competitors. Their inclusion in the unrestricted class gives Q<=H everywhere. The ordinary class contains V_1=w-K, a proper L1 lower member. Together with its upper bound F, this permits application of n1 to the entire class: Q is genuine h-psh with the EXACT inequality h+DQ>=0. Also Q>=V_t canonically for every t.

By n3, w is finite outside a measure-zero set. At each such point V_t tends to H as t decreases to zero, so Q>=H there. Thus Q=H almost everywhere. This is not yet the requested conclusion. On a small coordinate ball add one quadratic q dominating h, making Q+q and H+q psh. Their ball averages agree because the functions agree almost everywhere. The canonical ball-average recovery identity of n1 then yields Q(x)+q(x)=H(x)+q(x) at EVERY center x. Therefore Q=H at every point, including prescribed and additional poles. The raw supremum of the constructed V_t can remain negative infinite at poles; the canonical upper regularization recovers H there.

We have proved for EVERY continuous F, hence every original smooth F,

  P_{h,F}[u]=P_{h,F}[u]_I=P_h(F)

canonically everywhere, with min F<=P_h(F)<=max F. For F=0, zero is itself an unrestricted competitor and every competitor is <=0. Hence both zero-obstacle envelopes are exactly the genuine potential 0. The prescribed nonempty pole set shows that u is not boundedly equivalent to 0.

Separate original completion. A--D are proved for the entire stated explicit family without BMP or a positive-lower-volume assumption. The admissibility used here has been expanded: constants and convex sums are h-psh; each competitor class is nonempty as shown; continuous obstacles bound the families above; and their upper regularizations are genuine with the exact h-current inequality. No further mass condition is imposed.

It supplies no theta,u,F with unequal obstacle envelopes. It certifies no zero-lower-volume or unbounded-upper-mass geometry, computes no top-product mass and proves no unbounded-product passage. If a GIVEN positive h has a relevant zero lower mass or unbounded upper mass, these linear-current and integrability calculations still apply on that h; this is conditional applicability, not certification of such a geometry or its masses. No lower singularity volume for the constructed types is asserted. No literature priority is certified.

Thus E is respected: the restricted assignment is reconstructed affirmatively, while the universal implication and counterexample alternatives remain unresolved by this work. All original definitions and the full original completion criterion are retained in the input artifact.
